messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-10T14:12Z - SEV2 - Multiple GPU pods on svc-runtime-prod are failing with repeated OOMs and 'CUDA illegal memory access'. Paging pressure increasing on node gpu-47. Pager: @oncall-amber
oncall-amber: seeing it. svc-runtime-prod-redis-cache pods still up, but most gen workers restarting in a loop.
eng-runtime-lee: started tailing logs on gpu-47, attaching quick snippet:
```
[14:10:21] runtime: CUDA error: illegal memory access
[14:10:21] kernel: WARN: unaligned pte entry at 0x7f9b3c...
[14:10:21] containerd: oom kill (task gen-worker) pid=14321 status=0x9
```
sre-miguel: is this the pagetable corruption we saw two months ago? we had a hotpatch then.
eng-runtime-lee: similar symptoms but different stack traces. this one shows mixed 'unaligned pte' and 'pagewalk retry' messages. kernel trace attached in case it helps: `page_walk: retry, smmu fault at level 2`
infra-alex: i'm marking gpu-47 cordoned and starting drain of non-critical pods. will keep runtime pods pinned for repro.
oncall-amber: customer-impact? any 5xxs seen from upstream?
customer-success-jordan: a handful of customers reported increased latency and some 503s around 14:11-14:13. CS triage: two enterprise customers opened tickets.
eng-ml-rina: quick telemetry check - this cohort of requests had longer sequences (avg seq len 4096) and slightly higher cache-miss rate; possible KV-cache pressure causing memory blowout.
eng-runtime-lee: temp mitigation plan: 1) disable batching on canary zone to reduce peak token usage 2) fallback to cpu-quant model variant for remaining requests 3) cordon/restart gpu node after draining non-prod.
sre-miguel: propose immediate rollout policy: enable fallback route for prod traffic to model-quant-cpu for 10% of traffic then 100% if errors persist. engineers, can you flip that now?
eng-runtime-lee: deploying fallback rule now via console: `redwood route update --name svc-runtime --fallback model-quant-cpu --percent 10`
deploy-bot: deploy queued: route change #3421 by eng-runtime-lee at 14:18Z.
oncall-amber: after fallback 10% -> what's the observation window?
sre-miguel: watch 5m error rate and 1m p95 latency. if error_rate drops below 0.2% for 5m, hold; if not, ramp to 100% and cordon node.
eng-runtime-lee: 14:22Z: 10% fallback applied. initial error rate down from 2.4% to 1.6% (not great).
eng-ml-rina: adding a temporary cache bypass to reduce KV-cache lookups for the high-seq cohort, patch rolling now.
infra-alex: drain on gpu-47 completed for non-critical pods; gen-worker pods still OOMing on restart — stopping auto-restarts to avoid thrash.
oncall-amber: can we prevent noisy neighbor cross-talk? is this localized to gpu-47 or across racks?
eng-runtime-lee: telemetry shows similar but lower magnitude errors on gpu-51 and gpu-39 — all in rack-8. suggests something environmental or a driver/firmware regression.
sre-miguel: escalate to HW/driver team. @infra-alex please collect `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, and pci config from the three nodes and upload to the incident ticket.
infra-alex: uploading bundle to ticket #INC-2026-334 now.
eng-runtime-lee: added temporary canary rule to failover 100% to cpu-quant for affected customers while we root-cause. will send customer update draft.
customer-success-jordan: Draft to customers posted in #customer-updates: "We've detected memory-access failures impacting inference latency on a subset of GPU nodes; we've failed over affected requests to a CPU-backed model to mitigate user impact. We're investigating root cause and will update in 30 minutes."
eng-ml-rina: small repro run on isolated node shows: run with sequence=8192 reproduces `illegal memory access` within 60s. suspect race between page reclaim and kernel DMA mapping in SMMU scenario.
eng-runtime-lee: for long-term, we should consider lowering default max-seq or enforce KV cache pinning for large sequences; open a follow-up RFC.
sre-miguel: incident timeline notes: 14:10 first errors, 14:18 mitigation (10% fallback), 14:25 ramp to 100% cpu fallback, 14:40 node cordoned and under HW investigation.
oncall-amber: handing off to daytime oncall @sre-miguel for continued coordinate and customer comms. I'll stick on the thread for handover notes.
sre-miguel: taking over. action items: 1) continue hardware bundle collection 2) vendor kernel/driver escalation 3) prepare postmortem with tracebacks and memory maps 4) customer follow-up at 15:00Z.
incident-bot: UPDATE: SEV2 -> SEV3 at 15:05Z. Impact mitigated via CPU fallback; hardware team investigating root cause.
eng-runtime-lee: pushing a hotfix to avoid auto-batching for sequences >4096 as a temporary config change: `runtime.config.batch.max_seq=4096`
eng-ml-rina: note: model accuracy regressed ~0.3% under cpu-quant fallback for some prompts; flagged to product.
customer-success-jordan: posting update to affected customers: "We’ve mitigated the immediate impact by routing affected traffic to a CPU-backed model. We're actively investigating a GPU memory subsystem issue. Expected next update in 45 minutes."
eng-runtime-lee: will follow up with kernel trace and repro artifacts in the incident doc. handing off full postmortem draft to @sre-miguel once root-cause confirmed.
sre-miguel: closing active pager for this rotation, status: mitigated, ongoing RCA.
eng-runtime-lee: thanks all. :thumbsup:
